chain.label: ABX had no formal FEF program with adequate guidelines, training, or lighting/weather limits, and never institutionalized the 1991 pitch-down stall recovery revision
chain.trigger: the failure of ABX to establish a formal functional evaluation flight program that included adequate program guidelines, requirements and pilot training for performance of these flights

chain.label: ABX DC-8 training simulator could not reproduce the airplane's actual stall break (nose-down pitch/roll)
chain.trigger: the ABX DC-8 flight training simulator's inadequate fidelity in reproducing the airplane's stall characteristics

chain.label: Neither pilot had ever performed a clean stall in the actual DC-8; their only stall experience was the benign, low-fidelity simulator
chain.trigger: neither pilot involved in the accident had performed the clean stall maneuver in a DC-8 airplane before the accident flight

caused_by.evidence: Training for FEFs was informal and undocumented, and ABX had established no specific training or proficiency requirements for pilots conducting FEFs

the flightcrew's exposure to a low fidelity reproduction of the DC-8's stall characteristics in the ABX DC-8 flight training simulator was a factor in the PF holding aft (stall-inducing) control column inputs

chain.label: Undetermined defect in the stick shaker system; preflight and maintenance checks never verified the wing-mounted lift transducer under load
chain.trigger: Cockpit checks do not test operation of the lift transducer

chain.label: The stick shaker never activated during the developing or full stall
chain.trigger: the stick shaker failed to activate at any time during the full stall that followed

caused_by.evidence: the recovered components provided no evidence about the system's status and function. Consequently, the Safety Board was unable to identify the failure mode of the stall warning system

chain.label: The stall series was flown at night, well after sunset and end of twilight, following maintenance-delayed departure
chain.trigger: Sunset was calculated to be 1721 with the end of twilight at 1750

chain.label: Flightcrew ran the clean stall only slightly above the cloud tops at night with no visible natural horizon
chain.trigger: the flightcrew did not have a clearly visible natural horizon because of darkness and clouds above and below the airplane

caused_by.evidence: the airplane most likely encountered IMC soon after descending through 13,500 feet and remained in IMC until just before impacting terrain
no weather minimums were established by ABX for maneuvers performed at higher altitudes and beyond the vicinity of an airport, such as a stall series

chain.label: PF held the control column aft (5 to 20 degrees) to hold pitch attitude for a minimum-altitude-loss recovery instead of lowering the nose
chain.trigger: the PF applied inappropriate control column back pressure during the stall recovery attempt

caused_by.evidence: The PF's initial target pitch attitudes during the attempted stall recovery (from 10 degrees to 14 degrees) may have resulted in a successful recovery during his practice and teaching in the simulator
the minimum altitude loss stall recovery procedure places the airplane at a more critical angle of attack and drag configuration during the initial recovery from the stall

chain.label: Angle of attack kept increasing and the airplane entered a fully developed aerodynamic stall at 126 knots
chain.trigger: the airplane entered a fully developed stall

caused_by.evidence: An increasingly downward flightpath angle coupled with a relatively constant pitch angle resulted in an increasing angle of attack

chain.label: No. 2 engine (and briefly others) experienced compressor surges from airflow disruption at the high angle of attack, producing asymmetric thrust
chain.trigger: the CVR recorded sounds similar to engine compressor surges (popping sounds) that continued for 9 seconds

caused_by.evidence: The engine compressor surges that began at 1808:20 (as a result of the disruption of air flow though the No. 2 engine at the prevailing high angle of attack)

chain.label: Airplane remained stalled and underwent four roll reversals up to 113 degrees of bank while the PF continued applying back pressure
chain.trigger: The airplane experienced four roll reversals between 1808:25 and impact at 1809:38

caused_by.evidence: Each time the airplane developed a large nose-down pitch rate...the PF responded with additional back pressure, according to FDR data on control column movement
the inoperative stall warning system contributed to the accident by failing to reinforce to the flightcrew the indications that the airplane was in a full stall during the recovery attempt
by conducting these maneuvers without a visible natural horizon, the flightcrew was deprived of an important flight attitude reference that would have aided in their recovery from a full stall
the engine compressor surges...may have distracted the flightcrew during the critical early period of the stall recovery, when sufficient lateral control was available for the recovery

chain.label: PNF, informally serving as instructor/PIC, never told the PF to move the column forward or took over the controls, and lost awareness of the descent while answering ATC
chain.trigger: the failure of the nonflying pilot-in-command to recognize, address, and correct these inappropriate control inputs

caused_by.evidence: there were several indications of the PF's excessive aft control column inputs that should have suggested to the PNF that, as the PIC, he needed to correct the control inputs
the PNF did not escalate his verbal interventions or take over the controls...the PNF never told the PF to move the control column forward

chain.label: Airplane struck mountainous terrain in a 52-degree left-wing-low, 26-degree nose-down attitude
chain.trigger: impacted mountainous terrain in the vicinity of Narrows, Virginia

caused_by.evidence: the PNF's failure, as the pilot-in-command, to recognize, address and correct the PF's inappropriate control inputs were causal to this accident

chain.label: All six occupants (three flightcrew, three technicians) were fatally injured
chain.trigger: The three flightcrew members and three maintenance/avionics technicians on board were fatally injured

caused_by.evidence: The airplane was destroyed by the impact and a postcrash fire...The accident was not survivable
